author: Enlightenme
text:
Hi I have noticed that the terms UFL and LFL have been used more often prior to 2017. When we see two FLs on the chart, they would normally be indicated as an FL. (This is similar to our RBD and DBR exercise where we don't indicate any upper or lower RBD or DBR).

Why the difference? Is there any significance to the denoting of FLs? Possibly, an additional understanding of FLs?

author: Edge
text:
Hi EM, A FL occur occurs anytime a barrier is broken, retraces, and advances to hit an opposing TG. Ergo, it also Fails To Return. When price comes back in the opposite direction and takes out the FL, its once the MPL of the opposing FL is taken out that the new FL becomes a UFL or LFL (once it also hits its TG). Its Ping Pong back and forth.

RBDs DBRs Caps etc are exercises for your eyes to see the swings. These swings cannot be relied on to turn price. Nevertheless they are important because we can look at a swing and ask:

Should Price have turned here? Which of course we can answer because FO's can be predicted.

The only time I use a cap RBD/DBR as an actual trade is if its the MPL/LS trick. Which just looks like a little hiccup (FL/kink) on a higher scale but looks like an extreme MPL on the entry scale

author: Enlightenme
text: Hi Edge, From your answer, UFL and LFL doesn't denote any significant difference from FL. It is just that UFL are FLs above price and LFL are FLs below price. Thank you for your reply.

author: Edge
text:
Oh but it does.There indeed can be a difference.

The first FTR/Kink only needs to take out a "barrier" hit a TG to become a FL. The UFl/LFL NEEDS to take out an opposing FL

For instance I place a lot more emphasis on a UFL/LFL as a opposed to a standard FL. I still respect standard FLs for TGs but I am more interested in a FL that has removed a an opposing FL, therefore making it a UFl/LFL. Check out Salivans journal. He likes FLs which occur after a FTR/FL (he uses ones which which have also held price. Once the new FL occurs, thats also a UFL/LFL

I've just rewatched the lite course videos. and this thread relates to video no.2 "Where to look for PA" IF has clearly stated these points. Edge further reinstated them in "ignored levels' article.

By now you would know that we trade at the limits of a flag which are the kinks of a barrier which have broken, Failed to Return (FTR) and met its first target. Once the first target has been met. It becomes a Flag Limit (FL)

These barriers are;

- The break into or out of Compression (extremes of CP) - Highs and Lows (S/R) - Left shoulders (LS)

staurum wrote: my confusion: why would a Left Shoulder be created on a break of a FL?, then the difference between - a FL broken to create the LS - a FL after breaking the LS these two seems to be in a loop.

I actually placed this "FLs broken to create the left shoulders (not the FL created after breaking the left shoulder)" so as to make the reader confuse one for the other hehe here is what I meant: - a FL broken to create the LS means the barrier broken is an FL and as we know, once an important level is broken and assuming it hits target, an FL is formed in this case it is also an LS. - a FL after breaking the LS means the barrier is an FL in this it is also an LS and as we know, once an important level is broken and assuming it hits target, an FL is formed.
